AUTOSAR High-Level Design
EV Battery Monitoring and Thermal Management System
Document ID: EV-AUTOSAR-HLD-001
Version: 1.0
Status: Approved for demonstration
Purpose: Synthetic training document for the AUTOSAR HLD Document Analysis Assistant project.
1. System Overview
The system monitors battery voltage, battery temperature and state of charge. The BatteryMonitor software
component publishes battery status information. The ThermalController consumes battery temperature and
generates a cooling request. The Dashboard consumes battery status for driver display.
2. High-Level Architecture
The application layer contains BatteryMonitor, ThermalController and Dashboard. Communication between
application components is performed through defined ports and interfaces. The Runtime Environment (RTE)
provides the communication mechanism between application software components.

Page 2
3. Software Components
3.1 BatteryMonitor
BatteryMonitor acquires battery measurements and calculates BatteryStatus. It provides BatteryVoltage,
BatteryTemperature and BatteryStatus information to other components.
3.2 ThermalController
ThermalController receives BatteryTemperature from BatteryMonitor and determines whether cooling is required. It
publishes CoolingRequest to the cooling subsystem.
3.3 Dashboard
Dashboard receives BatteryStatus and presents battery information to the vehicle user.

5. Ports and Interfaces
5.1 BatteryMonitor Ports
P_BatteryVoltage provides battery voltage information. P_BatteryTemperature provides battery temperature
information. P_BatteryStatus provides calculated battery status.
5.2 ThermalController Ports
R_BatteryTemperature receives battery temperature. P_CoolingRequest provides the requested cooling state.
5.3 Dashboard Ports
R_BatteryStatus receives BatteryStatus. P_DisplayUpdate provides the updated display information.

7. Signals and Data Flow
BatteryVoltage and BatteryTemperature are measurement data produced by BatteryMonitor. BatteryStatus is
derived from battery measurements and is consumed by Dashboard. BatteryTemperature is consumed by
ThermalController. CoolingRequest is generated by ThermalController.
8. Functional Flow
1. BatteryMonitor reads battery voltage and temperature. 2. BatteryMonitor calculates BatteryStatus. 3.
BatteryMonitor provides BatteryTemperature to ThermalController. 4. ThermalController evaluates the temperature
and generates CoolingRequest. 5. BatteryMonitor provides BatteryStatus to Dashboard. 6. Dashboard updates the
driver display.
9. Dependency Mapping
ThermalController depends on BatteryMonitor for BatteryTemperature. Dashboard depends on BatteryMonitor for
BatteryStatus. CoolingSystem depends on ThermalController for CoolingRequest.

10. Architecture Relationships
The primary application relationships are:
• BatteryMonitor → ThermalController through BatteryMeasurementInterface
• BatteryMonitor → Dashboard through BatteryStatusInterface
• ThermalController → CoolingSystem through CoolingRequestInterface
11. Validation Rules
Every consumed data element should have a defined provider. Every interface should identify its provider and
consumer. Component names, port names and interface names should remain consistent across architecture
sections.
12. Revision Information
Version 1.0 is the baseline demonstration revision. Future revisions may add new components, signals, interfaces
or dependencies. The HLD analysis assistant should compare revisions and report potential additions, removals
and inconsistencies for engineer review.
13. Example Questions for the AI Assistant
• Which component consumes BatteryTemperature?
• Which components depend on BatteryMonitor?
• What interface connects BatteryMonitor and Dashboard?
• What is the functional flow from battery measurement to cooling request?
• Which component provides BatteryStatus?
